title: Carry an opaque collar around a curved guide without contact
instruction: Move the orange-handled collar along the curved guide from the blue support to the green support, Leave the guide passing through the collar tunnel, and centre the collar upright on the green support, parallel to the support, release it, and leave it still for at least one second. Keep the collar clear of the guide and its anchors; keep both robots clear of the fixture and each other. Finger contact with the collar is allowed. Keep the fixture in place.
context: A precision bench fixture tests keeping useful views while manipulating an object whose own walls conceal the guide clearance. As the collar follows the bend, the informative viewing direction changes. Any safe strategy is allowed; neither camera motion nor a particular arm role earns points. This extends the familiar buzz-wire mechanism with a deep opaque tunnel, rather than claiming that ring-on-wire handling itself is new.
setup: Original calibrated YAM station and three original320x176 RGB cameras,20 Hz controls. Coordinates x forward,y left,z up; table z0.7475m. A fixed cyan8x8mm square guide follows a90mm-radius semicircle centered at(0.22,-0.10),z0.83m,from-45 to135deg,represented by72 rigid overlapping segments. Two fixed12x12mm aluminum anchors support the ends. A bolted320x320x8mm base is centered at(0.22,-0.10,0.7515). Blue start and green goal polymer supports are60x80mm,52.5mm tall,centered beneath guide points at-10 and100deg; their tops are z0.8m. An80g rigid polymer collar has a48x48mm square through-aperture,80mm depth,60mm outer cross-section and four6mm walls. Its32x24x20mm orange grasp handle lies60mm radially outside the tunnel centre, joined by a28x16x14mm bridge. Pink6mm corner marks outline both openings. The collar starts resting on blue with the guide threaded through it; both arms are at original READY poses with open grippers. All part transforms, colors and physical parameters are in scene.json. Physical grading uses thin transferable contrast coating on designated prohibited-contact surfaces, clean reference photos and post-run inspection; simulation uses private contact-event memory without paint rendering.
scoring: contact-witness-v3. Any prohibited contact during the episode leaves an irreversible failure witness and forces0, including brief contact. Prohibited: robot/fixture, inter-arm, nonfinger robot/collar, collar/guide or anchor. Finger/collar and collar/support/base contacts are allowed. All nonzero outcomes require the guide still threaded through both tunnel openings and a complete final1s with centre displacement envelope<=1mm and orientation envelope<=2deg. Score1: tunnel centre within7mm of green target, axis parallel within7deg and a square face upright within3deg for the full second; green support contact and no robot/collar contact throughout. Score0.75: same goal interval without complete release/support. Otherwise0.5 for final angular distance to goal<=38.5deg,0.25 for<=82.5deg,0 otherwise. No best-ever score, prescribed arm role or camera-use reward. Invalid monitoring invalidates the trial. Physical witness: a new attributable transfer mark versus clean baseline; no contact-duration measurement. Full details and coating-control procedure in SCORING.md.
run_limit: 2,400 actions (120 s at20 Hz), including32 Dream history steps; successful completion may end early.
reset_notes: Fixed layout, zero object jitter. Restore collar to blue support at-10deg with zero velocity; original READY arms/open grippers. Clear score/contact history. For physical reproduction clean/reapply witness coating and take new baseline photos; use light-touch and separated controls to verify material sensitivity. See scene.json and SCORING.md.
fidelity: Original YAM rig and controls. Rigid compound collar and72 box guide segments; no deformation or damage. Private240Hz contacts approximate ideal transferable marks; no pigment is rendered and real coating sensitivity is uncalibrated. Pose checks sample20Hz. Contact margins can register force before visual touching. Same-arm self/table collisions are outside this task rubric. Demo uses known-layout waypoints gated by original RGB, not simulator object state.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0/2400 actions (120s), valid original-camera run with zero prohibited contacts. contact-witness-v3 scripted demo:1.0/980 actions (49s), RGB-gated known-layout route. First full-score state at872 actions (43.6s); video retains withdrawal and rest.
